data.narrative:
Peak Energy, founded by Landon Mossburg and Liam O'Connor, is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 9 comparable companies: 1 public (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy set—no subset of three or more companies met the filtering criteria for stage and valuation tier. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. This approach applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $65M total raised as a valuation proxy, consistent with typical Series A to subsequent-stage advancement patterns, yielding an implied valuation of $130M.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $110M to $150M, with a median of $130M. This range reflects a 70–130% premium to capital raised, anchored by the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent, stage-matched transaction data within the Climate & Energy sector and the reliance on a generalized step-up multiplier rather than peer-derived multiples. Any refinement would require either expanded peer identification in the same stage band or proprietary transaction intelligence from similar-sized Series A financings in the sector.
